name: server-lifecycle
responsibility: Starts, finds, restarts and stops the server of a checkout or a release, carries a CLI invocation's requests to it, and holds what the server process does for itself
description: Sixteen names on four entries: ./server (ensureServerRunning, restartServer, serverStatus, connectedBrowsers, stopServer), ./server-client (requestJson, stateInvocation, statedInvocation), ./config (archboardUrl, removedEnvironmentMessage) and ./server-process, what the server process does for itself: recordServerPid, releaseServerPid, reportStartupOwnership, reportStartupEnd, serverCodeState and staleFrontend. A server owns its pidfile by the exact bytes it wrote: releaseServerPid removes the file only while it still holds them, so a server that bound the freed port, or the winner of a concurrent start, keeps its record. The launcher makes the same check by pid when it cleans up after a failed start or a stop. reportStartupEnd is a first-call-wins latch in the writer: a process writes one terminal startup record, and a later report writes nothing. The pane rules and the messages a pane is sent belong to workbench (TASK-653.08).
